newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slumps 88 cts as bull run hits wall.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slumps 88 cts as bull run hits wall.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures went into a steep slide on Thursday, finishing down nearly 90 cents and finalling breaking the back of a four-month-long bull run.
December Brent last traded off 88 cents at $22.69 a barrel, $1.22 below its high for the day.

Dealers said the slide was led by a reversal in sentiment and technicals on U.S. markets where crude and gasoline led the way lower. December gasoline, expiring on Thursday, lost 5.7 percent of its value.
But they said news that two rival Kurdish factions had agreed to extend a U.S. brokered ceasefire in northern Iraq had also undermined the oil market.
"This is meltdown," said broker Tim Holmes at MeesPierson Derivatives. "It's more than your average correction."

Holmes said the slide confirmed that Brent, for the time being at least, had said goodbye to mid-October's $25 highs. Brent put on $7.50 in little more than four months but since has shed a third of that value.
Dealers said financial hedge funds helped drive prices lower as local speculators sparked computerised stop-loss sell orders.
"We went through some important technical stops and that triggered the hedge funds," said a broker. The break below $24 for December NYMEX crude was seen as particularly significant..
In Ankara U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau said rival Kurdish groups had agreed to extend a ceasefire in northern Iraq with a view to making it permanent.
The UN-Iraqi oil-for-food exchange was put on hold at the end of August when clashes made it unsafe for UN monitors in the region.
"I suppose this puts oil-for-food back on the map but that's not the real reason this market came off," said a dealer in London.
Earlier November IPE gas oil ended up $1.75 a tonne at $219, resisting early signs of Brent's eventual tumble.
The Brent/gas oil crack spread finished up 20 cents at $5.30.
But on the basis of Brent's close gas oil can be expected to open several dollars lower on Friday.
